profile_text.body:
Modular describes itself as a unified AI inference stack, covering everything from custom GPU kernels to production cloud serving on NVIDIA and AMD hardware. The company says its platform is built for high-performance, portable compute, with optimizations running from GPU kernel to API endpoint, and that the same model and codebase run across NVIDIA, AMD, Trainium, TPU, Qualcomm, Intel, ARM, and Apple silicon, as well as CPUs, GPUs, and ASICs. It claims 2x performance, an open source stack, and support for top open models. Modular was founded in 2022, is headquartered in Los Altos, California, and is a for-profit startup.

The site names the MAX Platform and the Mojo language as its core offerings. Modular says MAX runs more than 1000 models, including DeepSeek and Kimi, out of the box, with PyTorch-like model APIs, and that workloads can run in Modular's hosted cloud or a customer's VPC. The company says its forward-deployed engineers tune each deployment. Its team biographies cite work on LLVM, Clang, MLIR, Cloud TPUs, the Swift programming language, TensorFlow, XLA, TFRT, JAX, cuDNN, and CUTLASS, at organizations including Apple, Google, NVIDIA, SiFive, Tesla, and Kyutai. The site also carries a testimonial about bringing GenAI innovations to AWS customers.

Among the facts on record, California is listed as the company's litigation jurisdiction, with a count of 281.
